BiblicalUsage: Abagtha is named once, in Esther 1:10, as one of the seven chamberlains who served King Ahasuerus — the king sends him, with six others, to bring Queen Vashti before him wearing the royal crown. He never appears again.
TheologicalSignificance: A one-verse servant carries no doctrine, and I will not invent one for him. What his verse does is set the scene for the whole book: a king's command, a queen's refusal, and the chain of events that puts Esther on the throne — God working through ordinary messengers and palace routines.
